title: Medicinal cannabis | NHS inform
text:
Medicinal cannabis
Medicinal cannabis is the term given to medicines that contain
cannabis
. These medicines are used to help relieve symptoms of certain conditions.
Specific cannabis-based products are available on prescription in Scotland. They are only likely to benefit a small number of people.
It’s illegal to possess cannabis, whatever you’re using it for. This includes medical use unless it has been prescribed for you.
Can I get a prescription for medicinal cannabis?
Very few people in Scotland are likely to get a prescription for medicinal cannabis.
Medicinal cannabis may be prescribed for certain conditions, including:
severe forms of
epilepsy
in adults and children
adults with vomiting or nausea caused by
chemotherapy
people with muscle stiffness and spasms caused by
multiple sclerosis (MS)
Medicinal cannabis will only be considered when other treatments have not helped or are not suitable. This decision would be made by your hospital consultant.
How do I get a prescription?
Cannabis-based medicine can only be prescribed on the NHS by a specialist hospital doctor.
The specialist hospital doctor will talk to you about other treatment options first before considering a cannabis-based product.
Prescriptions for medicinal cannabis will only be given if it’s believed to be in your best interest and if other treatments have not worked.
Your GP can’t prescribe medicinal cannabis.
Possible side effects of medicinal cannabis
Medicinal cannabis can have side effects. Symptoms can include:
increased appetite
diarrhoea
feeling sick or being sick
feeling weak
behavioural or mood changes
dizziness
feeling very tired
hallucinations
suicidal thoughts
Reporting side effects of medicinal cannabis
You can report any side effect or adverse reaction to cannabis-based medicine using the
Yellow Card Scheme
. This can help the Medicines & Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA) identify new side effects or risks associated with medicines.
Include as much detail as possible, particularly any brand name or manufacturer’s details.
Potential issues with medicinal cannabis
Medicinal cannabis can affect how other medicines work.
It can also affect how your liver works, so your doctor will need to monitor you regularly.
Your healthcare specialist will discuss possible interactions with other medicines before you start your treatment.
